name: Sitebulb
tagline: Crawl an owned site and turn technical findings into prioritized, evidenced hints
verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Sitebulb, crawl an owned site and turn technical findings into prioritized, evidenced hints. The hard boundary is rule depth, visualization, reporting, javascript crawling, and agency workflow, plus crawl scale, rule depth, and operational polish.
coreLoopDIY: Crawl a user-owned site, inspect HTML and rendered pages, turn technical findings into prioritized and evidenced hints, and export a reproducible audit.
requirements: permission to crawl the target site
whatYouLose: rule depth, visualization, reporting, JavaScript crawling, and agency workflow
moatNotes: crawl scale, rule depth, and operational polish
ongoingBurden: robots handling, rendering, canonicalization, deduplication, crawl traps, rule maintenance, scheduling, storage, and false positives
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Sitebulb because a crawler is buildable; professionals pay for years of edge-case handling and reports they can trust with clients. The recurring cost buys robots handling, rendering, canonicalization, deduplication, crawl traps, rule maintenance, scheduling, storage, and false positives, not just the visible interface.

alternatives.name: Crawly
alternatives.desc: A free Mac crawler that turns nineteen issue types into a clean findings list and keeps crawl diffs.

facts.install: Download and install the native universal macOS app
facts.engines: A local MCP server connects to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf and other MCP clients
facts.dataFormat: Crawl projects and history live in a local SQLite database on the Mac; there is no hosted account or cloud sync
facts.gapVsPaid: Its nineteen checks and simple findings list are much narrower than Sitebulb's visual hints, prioritization and evidence-rich reporting.

alternatives.name: FreeCrawl
alternatives.desc: A desktop crawler with 200 checks, issue evidence and project comparisons; the hint engine is younger, not imaginary.

facts.install: Windows installer or portable build, macOS DMG, or Linux AppImage, deb or rpm
facts.engines: Optional OpenAI, Anthropic and local Ollama; optional GSC, GA4, PageSpeed, Ahrefs, Moz, Semrush, Majestic and MCP connections
facts.dataFormat: Local SQLite WAL project files (.seoproject), optionally AES-256-GCM encrypted; exports include Excel, CSV, JSON, XML, HTML, sitemaps, Google Sheets and BigQuery
facts.gapVsPaid: Its hint engine and visual prioritization are younger and less proven than Sitebulb's mature audit guidance.
facts.setupBlocker: The prebuilt apps install normally, but the macOS build may require bypassing Gatekeeper for an unsigned application

alternatives.name: LibreCrawl
alternatives.desc: Unlimited crawls and a browser dashboard with audits; prioritization is plainer, but the evidence is there.

facts.install: Docker Compose, or a Python environment plus Playwright
facts.dataFormat: Settings live in browser localStorage; each browser session has isolated crawl data that expires after one hour unless exported as CSV, JSON or XML
facts.gapVsPaid: It has no durable project history and presents much plainer prioritization and evidence than Sitebulb.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker or Python plus Playwright is required, and local mode has no authentication unless the operator adds it

alternatives.name: SEOnaut
alternatives.desc: Stores audits and sorts issues by severity; not as pretty as Sitebulb, equally capable of ruining your afternoon.

facts.install: Docker Compose with MySQL 8.4, then expose the web UI behind HTTPS
facts.dataFormat: Sites, crawl results and audit history live in the self-hosted MySQL database
facts.gapVsPaid: It produces a simpler severity list without Sitebulb's rich visual hints, explanations and guided investigation.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker, MySQL and a reverse proxy are required; its default exposed port is plain HTTP

alternatives.name: SiteOne Crawler
alternatives.desc: Crawls locally, calculates a quality score and tells you what to fix first; almost suspiciously on brief.

facts.install: Download a prebuilt desktop or CLI binary for Windows, macOS or Linux
facts.engines: Optional OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
facts.dataFormat: Runs locally and writes project results plus HTML, JSON or text reports and exports to the user's disk
facts.gapVsPaid: Its fix-first scoring is useful, but its prioritization and guided evidence are less polished than Sitebulb's.
facts.setupBlocker: None for ordinary crawling; JavaScript rendering needs Chrome or Chromium, or the one-time headless-shell download

rejectedAlternatives.name: RustySEO
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Looks like the obvious new answer; v0.3.9 and its own buggy warning say not for readers yet.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Lite plan and a single-site audit tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Sitebulb in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, Playwright, and an HTMX interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: crawl a user-owned site, inspect HTML and rendered pages, turn technical findings into prioritized and evidenced hints, and export a reproducible audit.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Require an explicit ownership or permission acknowledgement before a crawl starts.
Respect robots.txt, rate limits, canonical URLs, nofollow, redirects, and a configurable URL cap.
Collect status, title, description, headings, canonical, robots, links, images, structured data, and rendered text.
Detect duplicates, orphan candidates, broken links, redirect chains, missing metadata, and indexability conflicts.
Show every issue with affected URLs, evidence, severity, and a concrete remediation note.
Export crawl data and issues to CSV plus a self-contained HTML report.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out crawling sites without permission.
Deliberately leave out web-scale backlink or keyword datasets.
Deliberately leave out automated changes to production websites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
